title: How METR measures Long Tasks and Experienced Open Source Dev Productivity - Joel Becker, METR
summary: METR's Joel Becker discusses the developer-slowdown RCT, why familiarity/J-curve explanations seem weak, time-horizon trends and their possible compute-driven slowdown, and where agents still fail.

assertions.quote: And in fact, you know, we find that we find a slowdown.
developers will tell you that they were faster when they weren't.
how much is J curve explaining? I think it's not explaining that much.
some of the repos that I was helped the most with were ones that I was completely unfamiliar with
the humans not only need to spend expensive time verifying, but also like clean up clean up all the stuff.
if capabilities are measured by time horizon keep keep doubling, it does seem very very challenging to keep up with that.
if compute growth were to half, then time horizon growth would half.

verdicts.note: A contested economic modeling assumption; plausible as a near-term model but not empirically established.

assertions.quote: basically all the time they find that the models fall on their faces and suck.
computer use capabilities are considerably worse than CLI based stuff at the moment

verdicts.note: Through 2025-26 GUI/computer-use benchmarks lagged text and terminal agent benchmarks, and practical use stayed mostly CLI-based.

assertions.quote: It is okay at doing very trivial things and it fails at all complex tasks.
